notes: Sign in to the admin UI at /ui with admin and the generated UI_PASSWORD. Add models and create the API (virtual) keys your apps use there; the API is served at https://<your domain>/ (OpenAI-compatible routes such as /v1/chat/completions).
The master key (sk- followed by the generated MASTER_KEY, as LiteLLM requires the sk- prefix) is the proxy's internal admin key: keep it inside the server and hand out virtual keys instead.
LITELLM_SALT_KEY encrypts the provider credentials stored in the database. LiteLLM's production guide says to set it once and never change it: changing it makes every stored provider key unreadable.

The litellm-database image is the official build for database-backed deployments; with DATABASE_URL set it applies its Prisma migrations on start. STORE_MODEL_IN_DB lets models be managed from the UI instead of a config file.

v1.105.0 is the release main-stable pointed to when this recipe was written (same digest). PostgreSQL 16.15 (the official compose's major version, pinned) has its own named volume and no published port; the proxy keeps no other data on disk.

FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=* makes uvicorn honour the panel proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto. Without it uvicorn trusts only 127.0.0.1, but the proxy reaches the container from the Docker network gateway, so /ui redirected to http:// and the admin login fell back to plain HTTP (found live, RC-26). The port is published on 127.0.0.1 only, so the panel proxy is the only client that can set these headers.
The healthcheck is the official one (/health/liveliness through python3) pointed at 127.0.0.1. The database uses the panel database-memory default.
The admin UI shows a banner that environment-credential login is enabled: admin + UI_PASSWORD is one shared static admin login. Keep it private, or add named admin users in the UI for each person.
Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-26): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running, HTTPS, first login and a real-use check passed; every image ref below is in its tested list.
